schemaVersion: 1

name: gof-proxy
version: 1.2.4
description: >-
  Proxy in modern Java: a stand-in that controls access to another object behind that object's own
  interface — virtual (lazy), remote, protection and caching variants. Covers the central danger
  of making a network call look like a method call, how a proxy differs from a decorator, the
  self-invocation hole that silently disables @Transactional and @Cacheable, JPA lazy proxies and
  LazyInitializationException, what CGLIB cannot proxy, and safe publication in a virtual proxy.
  Use when a lazy-loading wrapper is proposed, when a remote call hides behind a plain interface,
  when an annotation on a self-called method does nothing, when instanceof fails on an injected
  bean or a JPA entity, or when authorisation is enforced by a wrapper the caller can bypass. Does
  not cover adding stackable behaviour (gof-decorator), changing an interface (gof-adapter),
  sharing instances to save memory (gof-flyweight), lazy loading strategy in JPA
  (orm-behavioral-patterns), or client-side resilience policy (circuit-breakers).

sources.section: Java SE 17 Proxy API; newProxyInstance restrictions, Object methods, duplicate-method exceptions
sources.verified: Invocation goes through the handler only when the receiver is the proxy; handler results are returned. Object equals/hashCode/toString reach the handler. Interfaces must satisfy loader/module/non-sealed/non-hidden rules; checked duplicate-method exceptions must fit all applicable declarations.
sources.limits: API contract; compile target 17, execution below on 25.

sources.verified: Return must fit the declared return type; null primitive result is rejected; undeclared checked exceptions are wrapped. The API does not automatically rewrite a returned raw target to its proxy.
sources.limits: API contract, with focused JDK controls.

sources.section: Spring Framework v6.2.11 JdkDynamicAopProxy.java invoke, lines 210–238
sources.verified: Compatible direct target self-return can be replaced with proxy, excluding Object return type and RawTargetAccess declarations. Embedded raw targets are not repaired. Dynamic target release occurs in the invocation finally block.
sources.limits: Pinned implementation, not a guarantee for every proxy/framework or a Spring runtime test.

sources.section: Spring Framework 6.2 documentation: proxy mechanisms and self-invocation
sources.verified: Subclass advice cannot override final/private/inaccessible methods; normal target self-invocation bypasses proxy advice, while AspectJ weaving differs. Objenesis can avoid invoking a target constructor a second time.
sources.limits: Versioned documentation branch, not pinned minor implementation/runtime.

sources.section: Spring Framework 6.2 documentation: @Cacheable and default key generation
sources.verified: A hit can return without target invocation; default keys derive from arguments. The skill's access-control consequence is an inference from this short circuit, contingent on required checks and actual advice order.
sources.limits: Cache-hit authorization/revocation guidance is a reasoned contract consequence; no Spring Security/cache integration run.

sources.section: Hibernate ORM 6.6 Hibernate API intro and unproxy methods
sources.verified: Lazy association representation depends on enhancement and polymorphism. Unproxy may initialize and fail without an open session for an uninitialized proxy.
sources.limits: Versioned provider docs; no Hibernate/database runtime or query count captured.

sources.verified: Monitor and volatile happens-before semantics support the lazy publication/guarding reasoning; correct synchronization alone does not establish application progress or lifecycle correctness.
sources.limits: Language contract; finite 24-consumer run is not a proof of all schedules.

sources.section: Java SE 17 Future get(timeout), cancellation methods
sources.verified: A timed get bounds the caller's wait. Cancellation is separate and does not itself establish interruption cooperation or a completed underlying operation.
sources.limits: API contract; no deliberately deadlocked process was created.
